questions.question: What is the sequence of tetrahedral intermediates during the saponification of a triglyceride with 3 equivalents of NaOH?

options.label: A
options.text: Direct SN2 displacement of fatty acids by sodium.

options.label: B
options.text: Homolytic cleavage into glycerol radicals.

options.label: C
options.text: Sequential nucleophilic attack of hydroxide on each ester carbonyl, forming three successive tetrahedral intermediates that expel alkoxide to yield glycerol and three fatty acid soaps.

options.label: D
options.text: Simultaneous cleavage of all three ester bonds in a single pericyclic step.

questions.correct_answer: Sequential nucleophilic attack of hydroxide on each ester carbonyl, forming three successive tetrahedral intermediates that expel alkoxide to yield glycerol and three fatty acid soaps.
questions.explanation: Saponification is a stepwise nucleophilic acyl substitution on each ester linkage of the glycerol triester.

questions.question: What side reaction occurs on the metal catalyst surface during partial hydrogenation of polyunsaturated vegetable oils?

options.label: A
options.text: Decarboxylation of fatty acids to hydrocarbons.

options.label: B
options.text: Complete polymerization of the triglyceride into plastic.

options.label: C
options.text: Reversible semi-hydrogenation allows the intermediate alkyl-metal complex to rotate and undergo β-hydride elimination, isomerizing natural cis double bonds into unnatural trans fats.

options.label: D
options.text: Oxidation of fatty acids to explosive peroxides.

questions.correct_answer: Reversible semi-hydrogenation allows the intermediate alkyl-metal complex to rotate and undergo β-hydride elimination, isomerizing natural cis double bonds into unnatural trans fats.
questions.explanation: Incomplete hydrogenation allows surface-bound radicals to rotate and eliminate, generating thermodynamically more stable trans-fatty acid isomers.

questions.topic: Bromine Addition Fatty Acid Unsaturation Assay
questions.question: Why does an unsaturated oil (e.g., olive oil) decolorize bromine water (Br₂ / CCl₄) while saturated fat (e.g., butter) does not?

options.label: A
options.text: Unsaturated oils precipitate bromine as a yellow solid.

options.label: B
options.text: Bromine adds electrophilically across the cis double bonds via cyclic bromonium intermediates to form colorless vicinal dibromoalkanes, consuming the colored Br₂.

options.label: C
options.text: Saturated fats destroy bromine by oxidation.

options.label: D
options.text: Bromine evaporates faster in the presence of oil.

questions.correct_answer: Bromine adds electrophilically across the cis double bonds via cyclic bromonium intermediates to form colorless vicinal dibromoalkanes, consuming the colored Br₂.
questions.explanation: Electrophilic halogenation consumes colored bromine as it adds across carbon-carbon double bonds, quantifying unsaturation (bromine number).

questions.question: What specific ester bond in a phosphatidylcholine phospholipid is cleaved by the venom enzyme phospholipase A₂?

options.label: A
options.text: The choline trimethylammonium bond.

options.label: B
options.text: The ester linkage at the central C2 position of the glycerol backbone, releasing a free unsaturated fatty acid (often arachidonic acid) and lysophosphatidylcholine.

options.label: C
options.text: The ester linkage at C1 exclusively.

options.label: D
options.text: The phosphate ester at C3.

questions.correct_answer: The ester linkage at the central C2 position of the glycerol backbone, releasing a free unsaturated fatty acid (often arachidonic acid) and lysophosphatidylcholine.
questions.explanation: Phospholipase A₂ exhibits strict regiospecificity for hydrolyzing the sn-2 acyl ester bond of membrane phospholipids.

questions.question: What is the key reactive intermediate in the enzymatic coupling of DMAPP with IPP to form monoterpenes?

options.label: A
options.text: A free radical generated by light.

options.label: B
options.text: Dissociation of the pyrophosphate group from DMAPP (dimethylallyl pyrophosphate) generates an allylic carbocation, which is attacked by the π bond of IPP (isopentenyl pyrophosphate).

options.label: C
options.text: An epoxide intermediate.

options.label: D
options.text: An organolithium carbanion.

questions.correct_answer: Dissociation of the pyrophosphate group from DMAPP (dimethylallyl pyrophosphate) generates an allylic carbocation, which is attacked by the π bond of IPP (isopentenyl pyrophosphate).
questions.explanation: Pyrophosphate acts as an excellent biological leaving group, generating a resonance-stabilized allylic carbocation that alkylates IPP.

questions.question: What remarkable single-step mechanistic cascade converts squalene 2,3-epoxide into the tetracyclic lanosterol steroid skeleton?

options.label: A
options.text: A sequence of four separate Diels-Alder reactions.

options.label: B
options.text: Thermal electrocyclic ring closures at 400°C.

options.label: C
options.text: A free radical polymerization initiated by oxygen.

options.label: D
options.text: Enzyme-promoted protonation of the epoxide triggers a concerted cationic polycyclization cascade through four contiguous rings, followed by a series of 1,2-hydride and methyl shifts.

questions.correct_answer: Enzyme-promoted protonation of the epoxide triggers a concerted cationic polycyclization cascade through four contiguous rings, followed by a series of 1,2-hydride and methyl shifts.
questions.explanation: Oxidosqualene cyclase catalyzes a breathtaking cascade: stereospecific polycyclization creates 4 rings and 7 stereocenters in a single enzymatic event.

questions.topic: Cholesterol Jones Oxidation with Alkene Migration
questions.question: When cholesterol is oxidized by Jones reagent (CrO₃ / H₂SO₄), why does the product contain a conjugated 4-en-3-one system?

options.label: A
options.text: The double bond is cleaved by ozonolysis.

options.label: B
options.text: The chromium atom directly moves the double bond.

options.label: C
options.text: Cholesterol decarboxylates in acid.

options.label: D
options.text: Oxidation of the 3β-OH yields a β,γ-unsaturated ketone (5-cholesten-3-one), which rapidly tautomerizes in acid to the thermodynamically more stable conjugated α,β-unsaturated enone (4-cholesten-3-one).

questions.correct_answer: Oxidation of the 3β-OH yields a β,γ-unsaturated ketone (5-cholesten-3-one), which rapidly tautomerizes in acid to the thermodynamically more stable conjugated α,β-unsaturated enone (4-cholesten-3-one).
questions.explanation: Acid-catalyzed enolization of the initial β,γ-unsaturated ketone drives double-bond migration into conjugation with the C3 carbonyl.

questions.question: What is the mechanistic role of cyclooxygenase (COX-1/COX-2) in the conversion of arachidonic acid to prostaglandin H₂ (PGH₂)?

options.label: A
options.text: Hydrolysis of arachidonic acid into four molecules of pentanoic acid.

options.label: B
options.text: Direct reduction of arachidonic acid by NADH.

options.label: C
options.text: Friedel-Crafts alkylation of the fatty acid.

options.label: D
options.text: Stereospecific radical abstraction of a hydrogen atom by a tyrosyl radical, followed by two sequential additions of molecular oxygen (O₂) to forge a bicyclic endoperoxide cyclopentane ring.

questions.correct_answer: Stereospecific radical abstraction of a hydrogen atom by a tyrosyl radical, followed by two sequential additions of molecular oxygen (O₂) to forge a bicyclic endoperoxide cyclopentane ring.
questions.explanation: COX enzymes utilize a tyrosyl radical to initiate bis-dioxygenation and cyclization of arachidonic acid into the cyclopentane endoperoxide PGH₂.

questions.question: How does aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) mechanistically inactivate the cyclooxygenase (COX) enzyme?

options.label: A
options.text: Aspirin oxidizes the heme iron from Fe(II) to Fe(III).

options.label: B
options.text: Aspirin transfers its acetyl group to a nucleophilic serine residue (Ser530) in the active site channel via nucleophilic acyl substitution, physically blocking arachidonic acid binding.

options.label: C
options.text: Aspirin coordinates to the RNA of the enzyme.

options.label: D
options.text: Aspirin dissolves the enzyme membrane.

questions.correct_answer: Aspirin transfers its acetyl group to a nucleophilic serine residue (Ser530) in the active site channel via nucleophilic acyl substitution, physically blocking arachidonic acid binding.
questions.explanation: Covalent acetylation of Ser530 irreversibly blocks the cyclooxygenase active site channel, preventing prostaglandin synthesis.

questions.question: What products are generated when spermaceti wax (cetyl palmitate, C₁₅H₃₁COOC₁₆H₃₃) is subjected to base-catalyzed methanolysis?

options.label: A
options.text: Glycerol and palmitic acid.

options.label: B
options.text: Methyl palmitate (a fatty acid methyl ester) and 1-hexadecanol (cetyl alcohol), resulting from nucleophilic acyl substitution by methoxide.

options.label: C
options.text: Palmitic acid and ethylene glycol.

options.label: D
options.text: Hexadecane and palmitic anhydride.

questions.correct_answer: Methyl palmitate (a fatty acid methyl ester) and 1-hexadecanol (cetyl alcohol), resulting from nucleophilic acyl substitution by methoxide.
questions.explanation: Waxes are simple monoesters of long-chain fatty acids with long-chain fatty alcohols; transesterification yields the methyl ester and free long-chain alcohol.

questions.question: What products are generated when spermaceti wax (cetyl palmitate, C₁₅H₃₁COOC₁₆H₃₃) is subjected to base-catalyzed methanolysis?

options.label: A
options.text: Methyl palmitate (a fatty acid methyl ester) and 1-hexadecanol (cetyl alcohol), resulting from nucleophilic acyl substitution by methoxide.

options.label: B
options.text: Palmitic acid and ethylene glycol.

options.label: C
options.text: Glycerol and palmitic acid.

options.label: D
options.text: Hexadecane and palmitic anhydride.

questions.correct_answer: Methyl palmitate (a fatty acid methyl ester) and 1-hexadecanol (cetyl alcohol), resulting from nucleophilic acyl substitution by methoxide.
questions.explanation: Waxes are simple monoesters of long-chain fatty acids with long-chain fatty alcohols; transesterification yields the methyl ester and free long-chain alcohol.

questions.question: What is the sequence of tetrahedral intermediates during the saponification of a triglyceride with 3 equivalents of NaOH?

options.label: A
options.text: Simultaneous cleavage of all three ester bonds in a single pericyclic step.

options.label: B
options.text: Sequential nucleophilic attack of hydroxide on each ester carbonyl, forming three successive tetrahedral intermediates that expel alkoxide to yield glycerol and three fatty acid soaps.

options.label: C
options.text: Direct SN2 displacement of fatty acids by sodium.

options.label: D
options.text: Homolytic cleavage into glycerol radicals.

questions.correct_answer: Sequential nucleophilic attack of hydroxide on each ester carbonyl, forming three successive tetrahedral intermediates that expel alkoxide to yield glycerol and three fatty acid soaps.
questions.explanation: Saponification is a stepwise nucleophilic acyl substitution on each ester linkage of the glycerol triester.

questions.question: What side reaction occurs on the metal catalyst surface during partial hydrogenation of polyunsaturated vegetable oils?

options.label: A
options.text: Complete polymerization of the triglyceride into plastic.

options.label: B
options.text: Oxidation of fatty acids to explosive peroxides.

options.label: C
options.text: Reversible semi-hydrogenation allows the intermediate alkyl-metal complex to rotate and undergo β-hydride elimination, isomerizing natural cis double bonds into unnatural trans fats.

options.label: D
options.text: Decarboxylation of fatty acids to hydrocarbons.

questions.correct_answer: Reversible semi-hydrogenation allows the intermediate alkyl-metal complex to rotate and undergo β-hydride elimination, isomerizing natural cis double bonds into unnatural trans fats.
questions.explanation: Incomplete hydrogenation allows surface-bound radicals to rotate and eliminate, generating thermodynamically more stable trans-fatty acid isomers.

questions.topic: Bromine Addition Fatty Acid Unsaturation Assay
questions.question: Why does an unsaturated oil (e.g., olive oil) decolorize bromine water (Br₂ / CCl₄) while saturated fat (e.g., butter) does not?

options.label: A
options.text: Bromine evaporates faster in the presence of oil.

options.label: B
options.text: Bromine adds electrophilically across the cis double bonds via cyclic bromonium intermediates to form colorless vicinal dibromoalkanes, consuming the colored Br₂.

options.label: C
options.text: Saturated fats destroy bromine by oxidation.

options.label: D
options.text: Unsaturated oils precipitate bromine as a yellow solid.

questions.correct_answer: Bromine adds electrophilically across the cis double bonds via cyclic bromonium intermediates to form colorless vicinal dibromoalkanes, consuming the colored Br₂.
questions.explanation: Electrophilic halogenation consumes colored bromine as it adds across carbon-carbon double bonds, quantifying unsaturation (bromine number).

questions.question: What specific ester bond in a phosphatidylcholine phospholipid is cleaved by the venom enzyme phospholipase A₂?

options.label: A
options.text: The ester linkage at C1 exclusively.

options.label: B
options.text: The phosphate ester at C3.

options.label: C
options.text: The choline trimethylammonium bond.

options.label: D
options.text: The ester linkage at the central C2 position of the glycerol backbone, releasing a free unsaturated fatty acid (often arachidonic acid) and lysophosphatidylcholine.

questions.correct_answer: The ester linkage at the central C2 position of the glycerol backbone, releasing a free unsaturated fatty acid (often arachidonic acid) and lysophosphatidylcholine.
questions.explanation: Phospholipase A₂ exhibits strict regiospecificity for hydrolyzing the sn-2 acyl ester bond of membrane phospholipids.

questions.question: What is the key reactive intermediate in the enzymatic coupling of DMAPP with IPP to form monoterpenes?

options.label: A
options.text: An organolithium carbanion.

options.label: B
options.text: Dissociation of the pyrophosphate group from DMAPP (dimethylallyl pyrophosphate) generates an allylic carbocation, which is attacked by the π bond of IPP (isopentenyl pyrophosphate).

options.label: C
options.text: A free radical generated by light.

options.label: D
options.text: An epoxide intermediate.

questions.correct_answer: Dissociation of the pyrophosphate group from DMAPP (dimethylallyl pyrophosphate) generates an allylic carbocation, which is attacked by the π bond of IPP (isopentenyl pyrophosphate).
questions.explanation: Pyrophosphate acts as an excellent biological leaving group, generating a resonance-stabilized allylic carbocation that alkylates IPP.

questions.question: What remarkable single-step mechanistic cascade converts squalene 2,3-epoxide into the tetracyclic lanosterol steroid skeleton?

options.text: Thermal electrocyclic ring closures at 400°C.

options.text: A free radical polymerization initiated by oxygen.

options.label: D
options.text: Enzyme-promoted protonation of the epoxide triggers a concerted cationic polycyclization cascade through four contiguous rings, followed by a series of 1,2-hydride and methyl shifts.

questions.topic: Cholesterol Jones Oxidation with Alkene Migration
questions.question: When cholesterol is oxidized by Jones reagent (CrO₃ / H₂SO₄), why does the product contain a conjugated 4-en-3-one system?

options.label: A
options.text: The double bond is cleaved by ozonolysis.

options.label: B
options.text: Oxidation of the 3β-OH yields a β,γ-unsaturated ketone (5-cholesten-3-one), which rapidly tautomerizes in acid to the thermodynamically more stable conjugated α,β-unsaturated enone (4-cholesten-3-one).

options.label: C
options.text: Cholesterol decarboxylates in acid.

options.label: D
options.text: The chromium atom directly moves the double bond.

questions.correct_answer: Oxidation of the 3β-OH yields a β,γ-unsaturated ketone (5-cholesten-3-one), which rapidly tautomerizes in acid to the thermodynamically more stable conjugated α,β-unsaturated enone (4-cholesten-3-one).
questions.explanation: Acid-catalyzed enolization of the initial β,γ-unsaturated ketone drives double-bond migration into conjugation with the C3 carbonyl.

questions.question: What is the mechanistic role of cyclooxygenase (COX-1/COX-2) in the conversion of arachidonic acid to prostaglandin H₂ (PGH₂)?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Hydrolysis of arachidonic acid into four molecules of pentanoic acid.

options.label: C
options.text: Direct reduction of arachidonic acid by NADH.

options.label: D
options.text: Stereospecific radical abstraction of a hydrogen atom by a tyrosyl radical, followed by two sequential additions of molecular oxygen (O₂) to forge a bicyclic endoperoxide cyclopentane ring.

questions.correct_answer: Stereospecific radical abstraction of a hydrogen atom by a tyrosyl radical, followed by two sequential additions of molecular oxygen (O₂) to forge a bicyclic endoperoxide cyclopentane ring.
questions.explanation: COX enzymes utilize a tyrosyl radical to initiate bis-dioxygenation and cyclization of arachidonic acid into the cyclopentane endoperoxide PGH₂.
